title: What is the area of the shaded region?
description: A rectangle eighteen centimetres by ten has two corner triangles left unshaded. The video finds the whole rectangle, takes away the two triangles, and gets one hundred ten square centimetres for the shaded region.
teaching_notes: One idea: find the area of a shape by taking away pieces we know from a bigger shape we know. Watch for students who use the wrong sides as the base and height of the corner triangles.

source: Figure it Out (area of any polygon, question 2)
video_script.why: The child applies the pieces we know method of the solved example, here by taking two triangles away from a rectangle.
video_script.substitution: Find the big rectangle and the two unshaded triangles, then take the triangles away.
video_script.anchor: the book's rectangle ABCD, 18 cm by 10 cm, with E on AB (AE = 10, EB = 8) and F on AD (AF = 6, FD = 4); the region FECD shaded
video_script.payoff_line: The shaded region is one hundred ten square centimetres
never_show: the answer before the answer beat
maths_rules: unshaded ΔAEF has a right angle at A, legs AE = 10 and AF = 6: 1/2 × 10 × 6 = 30 cm²
unshaded ΔEBC has a right angle at B, legs EB = 8 and BC = 10: 1/2 × 8 × 10 = 40 cm²
video_script.design: One rectangle all video. The unshaded corner triangles are found and taken away from the whole rectangle.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; rectangle ABCD 18 cm by 10 cm with E on AB (AE = 10, EB = 8) and F on AD (AF = 6, FD = 4); the region FECD shaded

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.rect: rectangle ABCD appears with 18 cm and 10 cm marked
marks.e: the point E on A B appears with AE = 10 and EB = 8
marks.f: the point F on A D appears with AF = 6 and FD = 4
marks.ask: the region F E C D is shaded with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='rect'/>Here is a rectangle eigh B C D, eighteen centimetres long and ten centimetres wide.
<bookmark mark='e'/>A point E on the top side is ten centimetres from eigh and eight centimetres from B.
<bookmark mark='f'/>A point F on the left side is six centimetres from eigh and four centimetres from D.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the area of the shaded region F E C D?

beats.on_screen: the picture holds still and the shaded region glows with its question mark

marks.stop: the shaded region glows in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the shaded region and the two unshaded corner triangles; the whole rectangle = shaded + two triangles

marks.pieces: the rectangle splits into the shaded region and two unshaded corner triangles
marks.whole: the line whole = shaded + two triangles is written
marks.take: the line shaded = whole − two triangles is written

narration: <bookmark mark='pieces'/>Use the same method as before, with pieces whose areas we know.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>The whole rectangle is the shaded region plus two corner triangles.
<bookmark mark='take'/>We can take the two triangles away from the whole.

beats.on_screen: Given: ABCD is a rectangle, AB = 18 cm, BC = 10 cm; AE = 10, EB = 8; AF = 6, FD = 4

marks.top: the distances along A B are written
marks.left: the distances along A D are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the rectangle is eighteen centimetres by ten centimetres.
<bookmark mark='top'/>On the top side, eigh E is ten and E B is eight.
<bookmark mark='left'/>On the left side, eigh F is six and F D is four.

beats.on_screen: To find: the area of the shaded region FECD

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the area of the shaded region F E C D.
<bookmark mark='rect'/>Step one, find the area of the whole rectangle, length times breadth.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Eighteen times ten is one hundred eighty square centimetres.

marks.tri: the unshaded triangle eigh E F is outlined with the right angle at eigh and the legs 10 and 6

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step two, take the unshaded triangle eigh E F. It has a right angle at eigh, so its sides are the base and height.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Half of ten times six is thirty square centimetres.

marks.tri: the unshaded triangle E B C is outlined with the right angle at B and the legs 8 and 10

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step three, take the other unshaded triangle E B C. It has a right angle at B.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Half of eight times ten is forty square centimetres.

marks.take: 30 and 40 are taken away from 180 and 110 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step four, take away thirty and forty from one hundred eighty. That leaves one hundred ten.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Check it, thirty plus forty plus one hundred ten is one hundred eighty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The shaded region is one hundred ten square centimetres.
